name: BBK (Bank of Bahrain and Kuwait)
legal_name: Bank of Bahrain and Kuwait B.S.C.
founded: 1971 (incorporated by Amiri Decree in March 1971; CR 1234 dated 16 March 1971)
regulators: Overseas branches: Kuwait and India (local regulators not identified in sources)
ownership_summary: Listed on Bahrain Bourse (BBK). Largest holders at 31 Dec 2025: Social Insurance Organisation (Bahrain, 32.97% = Pension Fund Commission 19.27% + GOSI 13.70%), Fincorp W.L.L. (Bahrain, 26.19%), Kuwait Investment Authority (19.20%); public 21.64%. Bahrain Mumtalakat is not named as a BBK shareholder in the AR or the Bourse list. A non-binding MoU for a potential merger with NBB was signed on 2 Nov 2025; BBK said on 21 Jul 2026 that talks were continuing.

government_link: Yes - Social Insurance Organisation (Bahrain social-security funds, 32.97%) and Kuwait Investment Authority (State of Kuwait, 19.20%) are state-linked holders (as of 31 Dec 2025); in the board listed in AR 2025 (before post-AGM changes) two directors were nominated by SIO and one by KIA. Fincorp W.L.L. (26.19%): ownership not established from sources opened; no source links it to Mumtalakat.
group_structure: BBK (listed) with subsidiaries CrediMax B.S.C. (c) (100%, credit card operations), Invita Company W.L.L. (100%, business process outsourcing; share purchase agreement to sell it to Silah Gulf B.S.C. signed, completion subject to formalities at 30 Jun 2026), and, via CrediMax, Global Payment Services W.L.L. (70% effective) and 973LABS W.L.L. (100%). Branches in Kuwait and India and representative offices in Turkiye and UAE. Brokerage is run as an in-house desk (no separate brokerage entity found). The potential merger with NBB (bh-nbb) is not completed, so NBB and BBK figures must not be added; NBB's consolidated figures include BisB, not BBK.

footprint: Bahrain: 17 retail branches, BBKPLUS digital branches, 3 BBKLite branches and 77 ATMs (Nov 2025); overseas branches in Kuwait and India; representative offices in Turkiye and UAE. 1,355 employees (2025).
customer_segments: Retail (mass market incl. approx 75,000 customers added from HSBC Bahrain's retail portfolio in Nov 2025, expatriates), premium (Al Wajaha), private banking and wealth (BBK Privé), SMEs, corporates, financial institutions, international banking (India, Kuwait).
business_lines: Retail banking; Wholesale banking (corporate, SME, financial institutions); International banking (Kuwait and India branches); Investment, treasury and other activities (money market, trading, investment advisory and funds management); BBK Privé private banking and wealth management; CrediMax (cards); Invita (BPO, being sold).

capabilities.wealth_summary: BBK Privé is BBK's private banking and wealth management segment: a dedicated Private Banker, Privé lounge, investment advisory and long-term planning, brokerage in Bahrain and GCC stocks and fixed income (foreign-currency bonds and sukuk limited to accredited investors), mutual funds (equity, bond and balanced; USD 10,000 minimum; 'top-rated fund managers', not named), ETFs, global real-estate deals and unnamed alternatives, plus estate/tax planning and insurance. Al Wajaha is the premium retail tier (salary BD 4,000+ or deposits BD 100,000+). In 2025 BBK hired a Chief Private Banking Officer (Aqeel Ghaith), said it is 'advancing its private banking proposition' for HNW clients with 'more bespoke and differentiated wealth solutions', and gave Privé clients T-bills and bonds through BBK Mobile. It acquired HSBC Bahrain's retail portfolio (approx 75,000 customers, completed 27 Nov 2025; HSBC private banking excluded) and holds funds under management of BHD 260.4m (fiduciary note, +28.5% in 2025). No AUM, robo or discretionary product was found; digital strategy centres on the ARRAY Innovation centre, open-banking work with Tarabut and a Google Cloud Universal Ledger core-banking pilot (July 2026).

private_banking.detail: BBK Privé: dedicated Private Banker, Privé lounge at Head Office, advisory, brokerage, mutual funds, ETFs, alternatives, portfolio monitoring, lending against financial assets; head: Aqeel Ghaith (Chief Private Banking Officer, joined 2025). AR 2025 says BBK is expanding the offer for HNW clients.

asset_management.detail: No separate asset-management subsidiary found. The 'Investment, treasury and other activities' segment includes investment advisory services and funds management (note 3), and the FY2025 note reports funds under management of BHD 260.4m held fiduciarily; fund products offered are third-party.

brokerage.detail: In-house brokerage desk (Bourse key-persons list names a Brokerage Desk manager and senior brokerage officer); Privé offers equity brokerage in Bahrain and GCC stocks and fixed income. A 31 Jan 2018 agreement with Mubasher Financial Services provided online trading via Bahrain Trade (search result only); current platform not confirmed.

digital_investing.detail: AR 2025: BBK Privé clients have digital access to T-bills and bonds through BBK Mobile for portfolio management. No in-app equities, funds or model-portfolio features found; eKey 2.0 launched on BBK Mobile in Jul 2026.

advisory.detail: Investment advisory and long-term financial planning for Privé and Al Wajaha clients; Financial Advisors handle mutual-fund and bond enquiries (the bonds page offers bond investment assistance for companies and individuals).

discretionary.detail: Privé page lists portfolio management ('ongoing monitoring and adjustment of exposures against agreed return objectives'); no discretionary mandate terms found.

model_portfolios_robo.detail: No model portfolios or robo-advisory found.

funds_platform.detail: Third-party mutual funds (equity, bond, balanced; USD/EUR; daily NAV; minimum USD 10,000; 'top-rated fund managers' unnamed) and ETFs; platform provider not named.

structured_products.detail: No structured products found on BBK wealth pages; Treasury page lists FX, hedging and liquidity investment solutions only.

private_markets.detail: Privé lists global real-estate deals and 'other alternative options'; no named funds or managers.

islamic_wealth.detail: BBK is a conventional retail bank; no Shari'a-compliant investment range found on wealth pages (Privé fixed income mentions sukuk; CrediMax issues Shari'a-compliant cards).

Collaboration to support open banking and explore digital-asset and tokenisation frameworks (AR 2025)
Exclusive banking partner delivering an integrated digital mortgage experience

Airport lounge access and promotions for Al Wajaha and Privé

initiatives.what: Non-binding MoU with NBB for reciprocal due diligence and negotiation of a potential merger; both banks appointed a multinational strategy and management consulting firm as joint adviser.
Completed transfer of HSBC Middle East Bahrain retail (consumer) business: assets acquired BHD 251.3m (loans 54.5m), deposits assumed BHD 256.5m, goodwill and intangibles BHD 33.9m (provisional).
Aqeel Ghaith joined as Chief Private Banking Officer; Innovation Center with ARRAY Innovation and Tarabut open-banking/digital-assets collaboration established.
At the AGM the Group CEO called the NBB merger a top priority and said completion in 2026 was still possible (press).
Received NBB's proposal on key merger terms including an exchange ratio; board review followed. On 21 Jul 2026 BBK stated discussions were continuing.
Announced with ARRAY Innovation a pilot of Google Cloud Universal Ledger in BBK's core banking (news listing title).
H1 2026 results: attributable profit BHD 42.5m (+10.1%); interim dividend 7.5 fils; investment and other income +66% to BHD 18.6m; Invita sale to Silah Gulf pending.
CBB approved purchase of treasury shares; daily 'Purchase of Treasury Shares' notices followed from Aug to Oct 2026 (titles only).
Executive-management resignation, appointment and 'Resignation of Group Chief Operating Officer' (corrective) notices filed 1-5 Oct 2026 (titles only; content not read).

opportunities: AR 2025 says BBK is 'advancing its private banking proposition' with 'more bespoke and differentiated wealth solutions' for HNW clients, under a new Chief Private Banking Officer (S5 p.9, S1).
Wealth shelf evidenced is third-party mutual funds (unnamed managers), ETFs, brokerage and bonds; no model portfolios, structured products or discretionary mandates found (S15, S16, S18).
Added approx 75,000 HSBC Bahrain retail customers (expatriate-heavy) in Nov 2025, with 'wealth management solutions' promised to them (S25).
Innovation agenda is partner-led (ARRAY Innovation, Tarabut) and BBK Mobile already offers T-bills and bonds to Privé clients (S5).
barriers: Merger with NBB under negotiation (MoU 2 Nov 2025; talks continuing 21 Jul 2026); platform and vendor decisions for the combined bank are uncertain (S9, S10).
Group COO resignation and executive-management changes disclosed 1-5 Oct 2026 (titles only) (S12).
Conventional bank with no Shari'a wealth range found (S16).
Core-banking and digital build is aligned with ARRAY Innovation / Google Cloud pilot (S13).

Mubasher Financial Services - Bahrain Trade online trading agreement, 2018; current status unconfirmed (S22)
